instruments.function: Open (cut-down) umbilical entry for the camera port under direct vision.
instruments.injury_potential: Entry injuries to bowel/vessels are the access-phase risk the open technique is chosen to reduce; no rate asserted in v1.
instruments.name: Hasson trocar (open-entry cannula)

instruments.function: Closed (blind) peritoneal entry and initial insufflation, the alternative access technique.
instruments.injury_potential: Blind entry can injure bowel or major vessels before any visualisation; modelled as an alternative, not the authored primary.
instruments.name: Veress needle

instruments.function: Camera and epigastric working ports; sites of this size receive fascial closure.
instruments.injury_potential: Port-site hernia if fascia left open (the closure microstep exists for this reason).
instruments.name: Trocar, 10 mm

instruments.function: Lateral working ports for retraction and dissection.
instruments.name: Trocar, 5 mm

instruments.function: Visualisation; the angled view is used to inspect the posterior aspect of the hepatocystic triangle.
instruments.name: Laparoscope, 30-degree, 10 mm

instruments.function: Grasps the gallbladder fundus and retracts it cephalad over the liver dome.
instruments.injury_potential: Serosal tear / gallbladder perforation with bile and stone spillage if traction is excessive; no rate asserted in v1.
instruments.name: Atraumatic grasper (fundus)

instruments.function: Grasps Hartmann's pouch / infundibulum and retracts caudolaterally to open the hepatocystic triangle.
instruments.injury_potential: As for fundus grasper; traction direction also tents the common bile duct toward the cystic duct line — the geometric substrate of the classic misidentification (T1).
instruments.name: Grasper (infundibulum)

instruments.function: Blunt dissection and spreading in the hepatocystic triangle; skeletonising the cystic duct and artery.
instruments.injury_potential: Mechanical injury to duct or artery if used beyond the visualised plane.
instruments.name: Maryland dissector

instruments.function: Peritoneal incision, triangle dissection and liver-bed dissection with simultaneous haemostasis.
instruments.injury_potential: Thermal spread beyond the visible tip can injure the bile duct without contact — the class II injury mechanism (lateral thermal/clip damage presenting as leak or late stricture, T1). The project design carries thermal spread as a single-digit-millimetre range (design/05); the primary biomechanics source is not yet consulted, so no number is asserted here.
instruments.name: Hook electrocautery

instruments.function: Occludes the cystic artery and cystic duct before division (two clips on the patient side).
instruments.injury_potential: A clip placed on a misidentified common bile duct is the Stewart-Way class I mechanism (T1); clipping is therefore gated behind the Critical View of Safety in the procedure model.
instruments.name: Clip applier with titanium clips

instruments.function: Divides clipped structures between clips.
instruments.injury_potential: Dividing an unidentified critical structure is the attempt-failing act in the procedure model (T1 class III mechanism).
instruments.name: Endoscopic scissors

instruments.function: Clears blood and bile, irrigates the liver bed, and provides blunt exposure.
instruments.name: Suction-irrigator

instruments.function: Intraoperative cholangiography through a partial cystic duct incision: delineates biliary anatomy and detects injury or retained stones.
instruments.injury_potential: Extending the duct incision during insertion can convert a partial incision into a transection; the step is optional and decision-gated in the procedure model.
instruments.name: Cholangiogram catheter with contrast

instruments.function: Contains the gallbladder (and any spilled stones) for extraction through the umbilical port.
instruments.name: Specimen retrieval bag

instruments.function: Purse-string closure of the cystic duct orifice from inside the remnant in fenestrating subtotal cholecystectomy (T4); also fascial closure.
instruments.name: Needle holder with absorbable suture

instruments.function: Pre-tied loop ligature cinched around the appendiceal base (simple ligation of the stump); the WSES-recommended closure family for uncomplicated and complicated appendicitis (T14).
instruments.injury_potential: A loop cannot seal a necrotic base: cinching it on non-viable tissue is the model's closure-mismatch error and computes a stump leak (T18 records the reciprocal practice - stapler chosen when the base's condition requires sealing healthy tissue).
instruments.name: Endoloop (pre-tied loop ligature)

instruments.function: Endoscopic linear stapler fired across the appendiceal base (gastrointestinal load), optionally taking a cuff of healthy cecum; may be used in complicated cases at the surgeon's judgement (T14).
instruments.injury_potential: A staple line fired across unidentified tissue carries the same misidentification risk as any division; in the procedure model it is gated behind positive base identification like every other closure.
instruments.name: Endoscopic linear stapler

instruments.function: Polymeric locking clips applied across the appendiceal base as stump closure - a WSES-recommended closure option alongside ligation (T14).
instruments.injury_potential: As for the titanium clip applier: a clip placed on a misidentified structure (here, the cecal wall at an unidentified base) is a mechanism injury, and clipping is gated behind base identification in the procedure model.
instruments.name: Polymeric clip applier

instruments.function: Atraumatic handling of bowel and of the inflamed appendix during exploration, exposure and variant mobilization.
instruments.name: Atraumatic bowel grasper

instruments.function: Skin incision, and the initial controlled opening of the transverse carpal ligament (T21: a small incision in the ligament is made with a scalpel or beaver blade).
instruments.injury_potential: The dividing instrument of this operation's master rule: a blade passed through an unvisualised tunnel divides what lies immediately beneath the ligament - the median nerve (T27 lists the median nerve among the structures injured iatrogenically at carpal tunnel release).
instruments.name: Scalpel, No. 15 blade

instruments.function: Longitudinal division of the transverse carpal ligament and of the antebrachial fascia under direct vision (T21).
instruments.injury_potential: Division carried beyond the ligament's distal limit endangers the superficial palmar arch, which lies typically 18 mm distal to the distal edge of the ligament (T22).
instruments.name: Tenotomy (Stevens) scissors

instruments.function: Retraction of skin, palmar fascia and the divided ligament edges so the ligament and the tunnel contents stay under direct vision (T21 names the Ragnell retractor in the proximal release).
instruments.name: Ragnell retractor (hand)

instruments.function: Handling of skin and palmar fascia during the approach and closure.
instruments.name: Adson tissue forceps

instruments.function: The completeness probe: slid alongside the median nerve after division to confirm the nerve is free proximally and distally (T21 names this instrument and this use).
instruments.name: Freer elevator

instruments.function: Protective retraction of the median nerve - and, in the persistent-median-artery configuration, of the artery - while the ligament is divided. The protection requirement is T21's (care is taken to protect the median nerve); the instrument choice is the module's.
instruments.name: Vessel (nerve) loop

instruments.function: Point haemostasis in the wound, including control of a divided persistent median artery.
instruments.injury_potential: Thermal spread beside the median nerve or its branches can injure them without contact; no spread distance is asserted in v1.
instruments.name: Bipolar forceps (diathermy)

instruments.function: A bloodless field for visualisation of the ligament and tunnel contents (T21: a tourniquet can greatly aid the surgery by minimizing bleeding and providing excellent visualization of the surgical field).
instruments.injury_potential: Pressure guidance exists in T22 (at least 100 mmHg above systolic, at least 250 mmHg) and is carried as technique text, not as a scored parameter; tourniquet pain and prolonged inflation are not modelled in v1.
instruments.name: Upper-arm tourniquet

instruments.function: Magnified epineurial repair of a divided median nerve or recurrent motor branch - the definitive control step of the injury-management pathway (the revision literature works under magnification and lighting for nerve repair, T27).
instruments.name: Operating microscope / magnification

instruments.function: Penetrating mesh fixation device (tacker) applying helical tacks through mesh into tissue - one of the fixation methods the HerniaSurge guidelines list (T36). Its placement is zone-disciplined in the procedure model: traumatic fixation is not placed below the iliopubic tract, and 2 cm above the tract is the extra-safety line for the triangles of pain and doom (T38).
instruments.injury_potential: A tack placed in the triangle of pain entraps or injures the lateral cutaneous nerves (T39); a tack in the triangle of doom endangers the external iliac vessels (T36, T39); higher tack numbers are associated with increased risk of chronic pain (T38).
instruments.name: Mesh fixation tacker (helical tacks)

instruments.function: Atraumatic mesh fixation by fibrin glue - the fixation family the HerniaSurge guidelines say should be considered to minimise acute postoperative pain where fixation is used (T36).
instruments.name: Fibrin glue applicator (atraumatic fixation)

instruments.function: Intraoperative nerve monitoring: stimulating probe with endotracheal-tube surface electrodes giving EMG confirmation of vagal, recurrent laryngeal and external-branch stimulation. An adjunct to the gold standard of visual nerve identification (T48; T42, Recommendation 42B) - in this module it demonstrates no gate criterion and accounts for no nerve.
instruments.name: Nerve monitor (IONM system and stimulating probe)

instruments.function: Right-angled clamp for passing ligatures around the thyroid pedicles at the capsule - the superior and inferior pedicle divisions of the thyroidectomy sequence (T44).
instruments.name: Right-angle clamp

instruments.function: Retraction for the neck field: strap muscles retracted laterally and the thyroid lobe rotated medially to open the tracheoesophageal groove (T44).
instruments.name: Thyroid (neck) retractor

note: Instrument catalogue for the theatre (design/05: instrument records carry function, appropriate use, and injury potential). Injury potentials are stated only where a consulted source supports them; otherwise the field carries a verify flag. Tissue-effect numbers are ranges with method tags per design/10; no point values are asserted.
